bounded_residuals.boundary: chunk relocation index table, 128 x u16 at 0x8009B2A8 -- 27 region-formed accesses based here
bounded_residuals.evidence: REFUTED LEAD: the `slti $s2,128` at 0x800295B0 does NOT gate these accesses -- it guards a DIFFERENT table at 0x800992A8 (lui 0x8009 / addiu -27992) with stride 4. The real gate at 0x80029750 is `slt $s2, gp[1280]`, a runtime count at 0x80082298 appended by chunk_pointer_relocate_index_fixup 0x8005D614 in a loop bounded only by a u16 header field, so CODE alone gives no useful bound. LAYOUT does: the next object is the matrix LUT at 0x8009B3A8, whose 64x8 extent is independently established from `andi 0x3f` -- so this table occupies at most 0x8009B2A8..0x8009B3A7 = 256 B = 128 x u16, max index 127 at stride 2 (255 at stride 1), against the 384/768 needed. Extent bound 256 B; reaching the nearest E16 window would need index 22916.
bounded_residuals.next_experiment: Watch the E16 table windows with a readwrite accessLog and confirm no event's PC lies in a function that indexes 0x8009B2A8; a hit would falsify this extent.

bounded_residuals.boundary: Accesses whose region base lies ABOVE the target window. Reaching the window from them requires a NEGATIVE index.
bounded_residuals.evidence: MAGNITUDE is what makes this sound, and it was measured rather than assumed (analysis/phase4_e16_signed_index_audit.json). Of the 2,922 accesses discharged this way, ZERO need a small (<64) negative index; 47 need 64-1k and 2,875 need >= 1k. The convention is not being asked to rule out an off-by-one -- it is ruling out an array running hundreds to thousands of elements BACKWARDS past its own base. 27.5% of the indices are signed-CAPABLE (lh, sra, subu, the sll16/sra16 short cast), but not one of them is asked to be even slightly negative. Same disclosed convention as region_provenance.c TIER 2. 0x8005D69C computes 0x800A6300 + (short)a3*4, a SIGNED short index -- the site that made this residual un-assertable. It is based BELOW its target, so it is not among the sites this convention discharges at all, and the measured risk set (small negative index AND not provably non-negative) is EMPTY.
bounded_residuals.next_experiment: Watch all three table windows with a readwrite accessLog across a campaign of per-level replays. Any write arriving from a base above a window falsifies this. One run (boot -> frontend -> Clover Forest) already passed: 7 PCs observed, none from a base above the window.

bounded_residuals.boundary: Accesses whose object has a distinct neighbouring object starting within 1 KB above it, where reaching an E16 window would need at least 10x that distance.
bounded_residuals.evidence: Bases are first clustered into OBJECTS (gap < 0x100), because the naive `nearest distinct base` version was retracted -- its median gap is 4 bytes, since adjacent bases are usually sibling FIELDS. Unconstrained the clustered version discharges 100% of the residual, which is the tautology signature; its tight-margin cases (ratio 1.0x) are exactly those where NO neighbour was observed for 12-18 KB, so the `extent` is a GAP, not a bound. Constraining it to a real neighbour within 1 KB AND a 10x margin keeps only the cases where the argument means something.
bounded_residuals.next_experiment: Watch the E16 windows across the per-level campaign; a write from a base whose object has a close neighbour would falsify the no-overlap assumption this rests on.

bounded_residuals.boundary: Accesses needing an index >= 1k to reach a window, against objects whose extents are not documented (4166 site-instances across the three tables, in 538 (base, stride) clusters over 33 base regions)
bounded_residuals.evidence: Median required index 10,977; the objects involved are pools and tables of tens to hundreds of elements. Still not PROVEN -- no element count has been read for them -- but its declared falsifier has now been executed in full: a 16-level any% campaign watched all three windows at 60 Hz, 1,930 events, and produced no unexplained PC. The only PCs found were the hoisted-load idiom, measured read-only and provably unable to form these pointers deliberately. This is asserted on the SAME basis the non-negative-index convention already uses: a magnitude argument plus a named, now-executed falsifier. It is a declared assumption, not a proof -- a replay shows what DID execute and can never show an untaken branch would not have written the slot. analysis/phase4_e16_campaign_verdict.json
bounded_residuals.next_experiment: Read the element count at each object's allocation or fill loop, largest cluster first (the 836-byte record array, the collision sector/grid working set, the sprite pool).

bounded_residuals.boundary: SCOPE: every earlier static figure for this row was computed over the 998 functions in functions_resident.txt, which cover 90.1% of the resident text. 32144 bytes in 12 gaps are reached by direct j/jal/branch AND majority non-zero -- the defensible figure for dropped live code. (Reachability alone gives 46020 B, but 20.5% of that is zero words: the largest such gap sits below $gp = 0x80081D98 and is small data, not code.)
bounded_residuals.evidence: Found by the campaign, not by inspection: a movie caught 0x80010BF4 reading a window, and that PC is in no listed function. The gaps are now censused -- 12 region-formed sites, ALL needing an index >= 16k to reach a window, 0 priority sites -- so they add no region-formed risk. analysis/phase4_text_coverage_audit.json, analysis/phase4_resident_gap_census.json
bounded_residuals.next_experiment: Re-run tools/text_coverage_audit.c whenever functions_resident.txt changes; a new CODE gap means new unscanned text and every residual figure must be redone. MEASURED 2026-08-04: repairing the list to 95.0% coverage (tools/repair_function_coverage.c, analysis/phase4_coverage_repair_impact.json) leaves the region-formed site set BYTE-IDENTICAL (5,810 both ways), so the hole cost this row nothing.

bounded_residuals.boundary: FORM: register-based (pointer-formed) accesses are invisible to the affine census, which only sees a lui-constant base. Repairing the function list would not surface them.
bounded_residuals.evidence: Bounded by materialisation instead: deliberate access to an address requires building it, and on MIPS that is always a lui-based constant. Scanning 100% of the text finds 5 sites reaching these windows, ALL already enumerated (815 near misses within 512 B). So no register-based access here can be deliberate. The 2 observed are the hoisted-load idiom -- 22 sites project-wide -- measured read-only. analysis/phase4_e16_address_materialization.json, analysis/hoisted_load_idiom_scan.json
bounded_residuals.next_experiment: Re-run tools/const_address_materialization.c against the windows; a sixth site, or any site not reducible to the enumerated set, falsifies this.
